official.deadline_note: Alumni of the Cusanuswerk study funding scheme face earlier internal deadlines: complete applications by 1 February for the spring round and by 1 September for the autumn round. A second external round (Verfahren II-2027) closes on 1 June 2027 with the selection decision in October 2027.
official.application_cycle: Verfahren I-2027 (registration deadline 1 November 2026, selection decision March 2027)
official.status_note: External applicants can register for Verfahren I-2027 until the registration deadline of Sunday, 1 November 2026; the selection decision is expected in March 2027.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The doctoral funding page publishes no tuition-fee coverage for the doctorate itself; tuition fees ('Studiengebühren') appear only as reimbursable in the context of stays abroad.
benefits: Monthly doctoral funding of EUR 1,750 granted independently of parents' income ('finanziell elternunabhängig in Höhe von insgesamt 1.750,00 Euro'), plus a research cost allowance of EUR 100 ('Forschungskostenpauschale in Höhe von 100,00 €')
Child-care supplement (Kinderbetreuungszuschuss) and family supplement (Familienzuschuss) on application
Health-insurance subsidy of 50% of premiums up to a maximum of EUR 170 per month where no compulsory statutory health insurance exists
Grants and advice for stays abroad ('Zuschüsse und Beratung bei Auslandsaufenthalten'); for stays abroad, stipend supplements can be granted and travel costs and tuition fees reimbursed

A multifaceted educational programme and a rich spiritual programme ('ein vielfältiges Bildungsprogramm und ein reiches geistliches Programm'), personal accompaniment and a large network of funded scholars and alumni
Compatibility with 25% positions in science: income from them is not offset against the stipend
eligibility: Outstanding academic performance and interdisciplinary interest ('herausragende fachliche Leistungen und interdisziplinäres Interesse')
Pronounced social responsibility, voluntary engagement, creativity, openness and capacity for reflection
Membership in the Catholic Church (applicants of non-united Orthodox or Oriental Orthodox churches may apply after individual review); a lived Christian faith and willingness to co-shape the Church
Abitur or a university entrance qualification entitling the applicant to study at a state or state-recognised university

German citizens: admission to doctoral study at a state-recognised university in Germany or abroad. Foreign applicants: admission to doctoral study at a state-recognised university IN Germany (funding foreign doctoral candidates abroad is not possible) and German language skills at C1 level at minimum

Applicants from a developing or emerging country in Africa, Asia, the Near or Middle East, Latin America or Eastern Europe must first turn to the Katholische Akademische Ausländerdienst (KAAD); a direct application is possible only in exceptional cases confirmed by the KAAD
requirements: Read the Merkblatt for the award of the doctoral scholarship thoroughly before applying (pages 3 and 4 list the required documents)
Apply with an exposé of the doctoral project ('Sie können sich für die Promotionsförderung mit einem Exposé Ihres Vorhabens bewerben')
Register online and upload a complete electronic package covering the doctoral project, academic performance and the personal career path by the registration deadline
Provide an academic teacher's reference (Hochschullehrergutachten); an English version of the reference template is published
documents: Documents on academic performance ('Unterlagen zu Ihren fachlichen Leistungen')
Documents on the personal career path ('Unterlagen zu Ihrem persönlichen Werdegang')
Academic teacher reference (Hochschullehrergutachten) - English template also published
Personal data form (Personalbogen) - published download on the official page
selection_criteria: Internal review and a first pre-selection based on all submitted documents, which can take up to eight weeks
Final decision by an interdisciplinary panel of university lecturers that also includes the Conference for Catholic University Chaplaincy (KHP) and the Cusanuswerk head office
coverage: Monthly funding of EUR 1,750 granted independently of parents' income ('finanziell elternunabhängig in Höhe von insgesamt 1.750,00 Euro')
Research cost allowance of EUR 100 per month ('Forschungskostenpauschale in Höhe von 100,00 €')
Child-care supplement and family supplement on application
Health-insurance subsidy of 50% of premiums up to max. EUR 170 per month where no compulsory statutory health insurance exists

For stays abroad: stipend supplements as well as reimbursement of travel costs and tuition fees ('Bei Auslandsaufenthalten können Stipendien-Zuschläge gewährt sowie Reisekosten und Studiengebühren erstattet werden')
No tuition-fee coverage is published for the doctorate itself
application_method: Online registration in the Cusanuswerk OmniBuS portal (https://omnibus.cusanuswerk.de/omnibus/register) and electronic upload of the complete application package
All documents must be present by the registration deadline and prepared for upload; a few days of upload time are granted after the deadline
Late applications and late documents - including academic teacher references and degree certificates - cannot be considered for the stated round
Applicants previously funded in the Cusanuswerk study funding scheme register informally by e-mail (Auswahl-Prom@cusanuswerk.de)
official.application_route: Register online in the OmniBuS portal and upload the complete application package (exposé, performance and career documents, academic teacher reference, Personalbogen) by the registration deadline.
official.citizenship_residency: German citizens: admission to doctoral study at a state-recognised university in Germany or abroad. Foreign applicants: admission to doctoral study at a state-recognised university in Germany (funding abroad not possible) and German at C1 level; applicants from developing or emerging countries must first apply to the KAAD.
official.international_eligibility: Yes, with restrictions: foreign applicants must hold admission to doctoral study at a state-recognised university in Germany, prove German at C1 level, and applicants from developing or emerging countries are referred to the KAAD first.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: No field restriction is published for the classic doctoral funding; the awarding body is the Catholic Church's talent development body, and Catholic Church membership (or individual review for certain Orthodox churches) is required.
official.research_requirement: An exposé of the doctoral project must be submitted together with the application.
official.duration: Maximum funding period of three years and six months, with additional extension options in cases of illness, maternity protection periods and child-rearing (the funding page states +12 months for illness or child-rearing and +3 further months for maternity protection).
official.description: The Cusanuswerk is the talent development body of the Catholic Church in Germany and supports doctoral candidates with a parent-independent stipend, personal accompaniment and an educational and spiritual programme. Applicants apply with an exposé of their doctoral project and are selected in two annual rounds by an interdisciplinary panel.
official.program_type: Doctoral scholarship (Promotionsstipendium) of a Catholic church talent development body (Begabtenförderungswerk)

not_confirmed: english_requirement (no English test or medium-of-instruction rule is published; only German at C1 is required of foreign applicants)
study_mode (no full-time or part-time wording is published)
tuition coverage for the doctorate itself (not addressed on the official pages; tuition fees appear only as reimbursable for stays abroad)
verification.notes: Monthly amount, deadline, eligibility, documents and selection procedure verified directly on the awarding body's doctoral funding pages; German wording quoted where the figures appear. The financial-funding overview page still carries pre-increase figures (basic stipend EUR 1,650, health-insurance cap EUR 100), so the current figures on the doctoral application page were used.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a monthly stipend of EUR 1,750 plus EUR 100 research money for up to three years and six months, awarded by the Catholic Church's talent-development body, and the current external round (Verfahren I-2027) closes for registration on 1 November 2026 with the decision in March 2027. You apply with an exposé of your doctoral project through the OmniBuS portal, and the complete package must be ready to upload by the deadline because only a few days of upload grace follow. Catholic Church membership and outstanding academic performance are hard gates, and foreign applicants must already hold a doctoral place at a recognised university in Germany with German at C1. The family, child-care and health-insurance supplements make it unusually family-compatible for a German scholarship.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Catholic doctoral candidates with strong grades, a doctoral place already secured and an exposé ready to submit - including parents combining research with young children.
application_readiness_checklist: Secure admission to doctoral study at a state-recognised university first; it is a formal requirement for the round.
Ask your academic referee early for the Hochschullehrergutachten on the official template, since late references cannot be considered.
Shape the exposé so that interdisciplinary interest and social engagement are visible, as these are explicit selection criteria alongside grades.
Fill in the official Personalbogen form and assemble the performance and career documents as separate packages well before the deadline.
Read the Merkblatt for the doctoral scholarship (pages 3-4 define the documents) before starting the portal registration.
common_rejection_risks: Late registration or late documents - the page warns that late items, including references and degree certificates, are excluded from the round.
Missing exposé or missing academic teacher reference, the two documents the process is built around.
Failing the Church membership or lived-faith requirement, or applying from a developing or emerging country without the prior KAAD confirmation.
Foreign applicants without a doctoral place at a German state-recognised university or with German below C1.
Thin evidence of voluntary engagement, creativity and interdisciplinary interest beyond academic grades.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition is not covered (German public universities generally charge no doctoral tuition, but semester contributions apply); relocation, visa costs and conference or research travel outside approved stays abroad must be funded privately beyond the stipend and supplements.
document_audit: Use the published Hochschullehrergutachten template (German and English versions) instead of a free-form reference letter.
The Personalbogen is an official downloadable form - complete it rather than substituting a plain CV.
Documents on academic performance and on the personal career path are separate required packages; do not merge them into one file.
The exposé is the core document; the Merkblatt's pages 3-4 spell out what it must contain.
alerts: Verfahren I-2027 registration closes on Sunday, 1 November 2026 - only a few weeks after the verification date; the next external round is 1 June 2027 with the decision in October 2027.
Only a few days of upload time follow the registration deadline, so the full package must be finished beforehand.
Internal pre-selection can take up to eight weeks before you hear anything; do not chase by phone.
Alumni of the Cusanuswerk study funding scheme have earlier internal deadlines (1 February and 1 September) and apply informally by e-mail, not through the public portal.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register in the OmniBuS portal, receive further instructions by e-mail, upload the complete package within the short post-deadline upload window, then await internal pre-selection (up to eight weeks) and the interdisciplinary panel decision.
